subject: Mid-cycle GPU burst add-on and slice billing — VAT routing question
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fyrecom.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:23:00Z
Subject: Short mid-cycle question: GPU burst add-on (PO attached)

Hi Sofia,

We're running a campaign next week and need a temporary +8 GPU burst for two weeks (10/12 - 10/25). I've attached our PO (FYRECOM_PO_5582.pdf). Two quick questions before we greenlight:

1) How will Redwood bill this mid-cycle add-on? Do you do a day-pro rata or a slice billing where we get an interim invoice for the exact days?
2) We're EU-based (Ireland). What's the VAT treatment — do we need to provide a VAT ID or will you charge VAT on the interim?

Can you confirm by EOD today? Prefer not to impact the scheduled deployment.

Thanks,
Liam
Head of Platform — FyreCom
liam@fyrecom.com

Attachment: FYRECOM_PO_5582.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fyrecom.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T10:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Short mid-cycle question: GPU burst add-on (PO attached)

Hi Liam — thanks for the PO and heads up. Short answers and next steps below.

Summary:
- Billing model: we can issue an interim (pro-rated) invoice that covers only 10/12–10/25; this is our usual approach for Dedicated/Dedicated add-ons when customers request an isolated burst. That invoice will reflect the exact token of days (daily proration) and any applicable one-time setup.
- VAT: For B2B customers in the EU with a valid VAT ID, we apply reverse charge (net invoice, VAT not charged by Redwood). If we don’t have a validated VAT ID on file, our system will default to charging VAT; we can adjust retroactively if you supply the VAT ID and it validates.

I've run a quick estimate and attached the prorate_calc_20261007.csv — this is an itemized slice: daily rate * 14 days + one-time warmup fee. Grace from Billing is looped in to confirm invoice timing and whether you prefer an immediate interim invoice or to have the charge netted on your next monthly statement.

Action items:
- Liam: confirm VAT ID to ensure reverse charge (reply or send to ap@redwood.com).
- Grace: please confirm whether we should generate an interim PDF invoice (preferred for PO match) and include a payment link.

I'll hold the burst until we confirm the billing flow.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Attachment: prorate_calc_20261007.csv

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fyrecom.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Short mid-cycle question: GPU burst add-on (PO attached)

Hi Liam and Sofia — finance here. Quick notes on process and timing so everyone is aligned: 

- We can issue an interim invoice dated 10/12 that covers 10/12–10/25 and attach it to PO FYRECOM_PO_5582. Interim invoices are generated as a separate PDF that can be used for AP matching.
- Payment terms: Net 30 by default; if you need a shorter SLA we can surface a payment link for card/ACH to accelerate.
- VAT routing: send the VAT ID to ap@redwood.com; once validated we will mark the invoice as reverse-charge (net). If validation happens after we issue, we will reissue a corrected invoice and credit the VAT portion.
- Accounting note: because this is a mid-cycle add-on, we do day-level proration; rounding is to cents per-line, with a single line summarizing the add-on period. I've attached the standard interim invoice template to expedite processing.

If you want the burst to start without delay, confirm (a) VAT ID or that you accept VAT charged now and (b) whether AP prefers an invoice PDF or the charge on the monthly statement.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Billing Manager — Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com

Attachment: interim_invoice_template.pdf
